However, decades of work in behavioral economics have questioned the validity of both foundations. Meanwhile, computational neuroscience has contributed a modernized 'dual process' account of decision-making where model-free (MF) reinforcement learning trades off with model-based (MB) reinforcement learning. The former captures habitual and procedural learning while the latter captures choices taken via explicit planning and deduction.
